mt_madison_river_area.blurb: A cluster of small crags and boulder fields strung along the Madison River in southwest Montana, a short run west of Bozeman near Bear Trap Canyon. Bouldering makes up more than half of the climbing, with problems spread evenly from V0 up to V9, and a solid number of trad routes sits beside a smaller set of sport lines and top ropes. Rope climbs run from moderate to hard, with most falling between 5.6 and 5.10. The rock is gneiss, and it can be weak and brittle, so handle holds with care. Crags here sit low and stay fairly sunny and warm, which makes them a useful winter option. Neat Rock Area, Bear Trap Road Routes and Winter Wall are the biggest pieces.

mi_grand_ledge_aka_oak_park.blurb: A riverside sandstone cliff line in the town of Grand Ledge, Michigan, and the only established outdoor crag in the state's Lower Peninsula. The rock is soft and brittle, which is why climbing here has long leaned on top ropes rather than leading, though the best-worn lines hold up well. Bouldering is the larger share, with problems from V0 to V10 and a fairly even spread through the middle grades, while the top-rope lines range from easy to very hard, mostly 5.9 to 5.11. The cliff faces south, catches sun for most of the day and is largely sheltered from wind. Evenings and weekends in good weather are busy and friendly, with many ropes hanging. Separate bouldering and routes sections make up the area.

vt_top_of_the_notch_boulders.blurb: A large boulder field at the high point of the pass through Smugglers' Notch in northern Vermont, holding well over two hundred problems, all of them bouldering. Grades stretch from the very easiest up past V10, with the heaviest concentration between V1 and V3 and a healthy supply of hard problems above V7. The stone is slick schist, which turns slippery in rain and in heat and needs time to dry after a shower. The field is spread across more than twenty separate boulders and clusters; the 2020 Landslide Boulders, The Asteroid, B.F.B. and Backyard Boulder are the largest, and the landslide group is a brand-new addition to the area.

az_granite_gardens.blurb: Part of the Granite Dells, a landscape of rounded desert granite just north and east of Prescott in central Arizona, at around 5,000 feet. The stone is medium-grained and a little grainy in places. Trad leads outnumber sport routes by roughly two to one, and a few top ropes and boulder problems round things out. Grades run from easy up to 5.12, with the bulk in the 5.7 to 5.11 range and the busiest stretch around 5.10 and 5.11, so there is plenty for strong climbers and a fair share of moderates. Two main sub-areas hold almost everything: the High Rappel Area, the larger one, and The Oasis, with The Waning Wall a small extra.

ma_quincy_quarries.blurb: A set of old granite quarries in Quincy, southeast of Boston, with at least twenty faces and craglets lettered by wall. Top-roping dominates, followed by a good number of trad lines, some boulder problems and only a few sport routes. Grades run from easy to 5.12, with most climbs between 5.5 and 5.10, so beginners and intermediates are well served. Walls reach up to about 90 feet, but most top ropes are well under 50. Slab and vertical face climbing on small holds is the norm, and spray paint covers much of the rock, making the lower sections notably slick. C Wall, M Wall and Swingles Quarry are among the larger walls. Many lines are short and squeezed together, with variations.

nt_yellowknife.blurb: A small handful of crags and boulders in and around the capital of the Northwest Territories. Bouldering makes up most of the climbing, mainly at the easy end, with plenty of V0 to V2 problems and a thinner tail of harder ones up to V5. Roped climbing is a minority, split between sport, trad and top rope, running from 5.5 to the low 5.12s with most in the 5.8 to 5.11 range, plus a few ice lines. The outdoor season is short, from about mid-May to early October, under fairly mild, dry weather. Cameron Falls and Hidden Lake Territorial Park is the biggest zone, followed by The Ravine, with Frame Lake and Tin Can Hill next in size.
